page.layout: One page of running text in one column; below the text, footnotes in smaller type in full lines, each keyed by a superscript letter (l, k, m, n) to the text. Running head at top with page number at left.

main_text.p: Paulus Burgensis, who expounding those words of David, "Thyl mercy, O Lord, is in heaven," or, reacheth unto the heavens, writeth thus: "Nok man according to the common law can merit by condignity the glory of heaven. Whence the apostle saith in the eighth chapter to the Romans, that the sufferings of this time are not worthy to be compared with the future glory which shall be re-vealed in us. And so it is manifest that in heaven most of all the mercy of God shineth forth in the blessed." The other is Thomas Walden, who living in England the same time that the other did in Spain, professeth plainly his dislike of that saying: "thatl a man by his merits is worthy of the kingdom of heaven, or this grace or that glory; howsoever certain schoolmen, that they might so speak, had invented the terms of condignity and congruity." But "Im repute him," saith he, "the sounder divine, the more faithful Catholic, and more consonant with the holy Scriptures, who doth simply deny such merit, and with the qualification of the apostle and of the Scrip-tures, confesseth, that simply no man meriteth the kingdom of heaven, but by the grace of God or will of the giver; asn all the former saints, until the late schoolmen, and the universal Church hath written."
Out of which words of his you may further observe both the time when, and the persons by whom this inno-vation was made in these latter days of the Church;

{k} Gloriam coelestem nullus de condigno secundum legem communem meretur. Unde apostolus ad Rom. cap. 8. Non sunt condignae passiones huius seculi ad futuram gloriam, quae revelabitur in nobis; et sic manifestum est, quod in coelo maxime relucet misericordia Dei in beatis. Paul. Burgens. addit. ad Lyran. in Psal. 35.

{l} Quod homo ex meritis est dignus regno coelorum, aut hac gratia vel illa gloria, quamvis quidam scholastici invenerunt ad hoc dicendum terminos de condigno et congruo. Waldens. tom. 3. de sacramentalib. tit. 1. cap. 7.

{m} Reputo igitur saniorem theologum, fideliorem catholicum, et scripturis sanctis magis concordem; qui tale meritum simpliciter abnegat, et cum modificatione apostoli et scripturarum concedit quia simpliciter quis non meretur regnum coelorum, sed ex gratia Dei aut voluntate largitoris. Ibid.
{n} Sicut omnes sancti priores usque ad recentes scholasticos et communis scripsit Ecclesia. Ibid.

page.notes: The footnote marks l, k, m, n are superscript in the text; footnote letters are rendered here as printed in superscript (l = 1 in the scan for the first note, which is a numeral mark). The superscript in "Thy" and "that" appears as a numeral 1 in the scan and is transcribed as the footnote mark. Footnote "l" for Psalm 36 and the second "l" note are both printed with this mark. Long s and printed hyphens are as in the scan; ligatures in the footnotes are reproduced as printed where legible.
